# Part A: Data Wrangling
**Construction of the merged_data Dataset used for Analysis ** 

The first section outlines the preprocessing and integration of clinical data used for evaluating diagnostic and risk markers of pulmonary embolism (PE). The dataset comprises of 366 total patients and two cohorts:

- **Case Group**: Patients diagnosed with PE. (n = 176) 
- **Control Group**: Patients evaluated for PE not diagnosed. (n = 190)

The objectives of this preparatory phase were:  
1. To merge and clean raw case/control datasets.  
2. To derive clinically relevant variables.   
3. To ensure consistent labeling and structure for statistical modeling.  
4. To identify type of missing data (MCAR, MAR, MNAR) and carry out imputation or complete case analysis.

```{r}
full_data <- "desert_valley.xlsx"
cases <- read_excel(full_data, sheet = 1)
controls <- read_excel(full_data, sheet = 2)
```

### Derived Variables for Clinical Interpretation
To improve the clinical interpretability of the dataset, five new variables were created. These transformations were applied separately to the case and control cohorts to support consistent risk stratification across the study population.

1. **Systolic** and **Diastolic** blood pressure values were extracted by parsing the original `blood_pressure` field, which recorded values in a combined "systolic/diastolic" format.

2. **BMI Marker** (`bmi_marker`) was generated by categorizing the continuous Body Mass Index (BMI) variable into six clinically recognized categories: *Underweight*, *Normal*, *Overweight*, *Obesity Class I*, *Obesity Class II*, and *Obesity Class III*.

3. **Heart Rate Category** (`heart_rate_geneva`) was derived in accordance with the Revised Geneva Score for pulmonary embolism. Heart rate values were categorized as follows:
  - Score **3** for heart rates ≥ 95 bpm
  - Score **2** for heart rates between 75 and 94 bpm
  - Score **1** for heart rates < 75 bpm
  
4. **Age Group** (`age_group`) was created by categorizing the continuous `age` variable into seven age brackets: *19–30*, *31–40*, *41–50*, *51–60*, *61–70*, *71–80*, and *81+*. 

```{r}
cases$heart_rate_geneva <- ifelse(
  cases$heart_rate >= 95, 3,
  ifelse(cases$heart_rate >= 75 & cases$heart_rate <= 94, 2, 1)
)

controls$heart_rate_geneva <- ifelse(
  controls$heart_rate >= 95, 3,
  ifelse(controls$heart_rate >= 75 & controls$heart_rate <= 94, 2, 1)
)
```

```{r}
bp_split_cases <- strsplit(cases$blood_pressure, "/")
cases$systolic <- as.numeric(sapply(bp_split_cases, `[`, 1))
cases$diastolic <- as.numeric(sapply(bp_split_cases, `[`, 2))

bp_split_controls <- strsplit(controls$blood_pressure, "/")
controls$systolic <- as.numeric(sapply(bp_split_controls, `[`, 1))
controls$diastolic <- as.numeric(sapply(bp_split_controls, `[`, 2))

cases$blood_pressure <- NULL
controls$blood_pressure <- NULL
```

```{r}
cases$bmi_marker <- cut(
  cases$bmi,
  breaks = c(-Inf, 18.5, 24.9, 29.9, 34.9, 39.9, Inf),
  labels = c(
    "Underweight", 
    "Normal", 
    "Overweight", 
    "Obesity Class 1", 
    "Obesity Class 2", 
    "Obesity Class 3"
  ),
  right = TRUE
)

controls$bmi_marker <- cut(
  controls$bmi,
  breaks = c(-Inf, 18.5, 24.9, 29.9, 34.9, 39.9, Inf),
  labels = c(
    "Underweight", 
    "Normal", 
    "Overweight", 
    "Obesity Class 1", 
    "Obesity Class 2", 
    "Obesity Class 3"
  ),
  right = TRUE
)
```

```{r}
cases$age_group <- cut(
  cases$age,
  breaks = c(18, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 100),
  labels = c("19–30", "31–40", "41–50", "51–60", "61–70", "71–80", "81+"),
  right = TRUE,
  include.lowest = TRUE
)

controls$age_group <- cut(
  controls$age,
  breaks = c(18, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 100),
  labels = c("19–30", "31–40", "41–50", "51–60", "61–70", "71–80", "81+"),
  right = TRUE,
  include.lowest = TRUE
)
```


### Binary Variable Standardization

All binary (2 levels) variables were standardized to follow consistent labeling. In the original dataset, some binary fields used numeric encodings where:  
  - `1` indicated *Yes*,  
  - `2` indicated *No*,  
  - `3` denoted missing entries.  

  In the new refined dataset:  
  - Values coded as `2` were recoded as `0` (*No*),  
  - Values coded as `3` were recoded as `NA` (*Missing*),  
  - All binary variables were converted to factors with levels: `0 = No`, `1 = Yes`, `NA = Missing`.  

```{r}
clean_binary_variable <- function(df, varname) {
  df[[varname]][df[[varname]] == 3] <- NA
  df[[varname]] <- factor(ifelse(df[[varname]] == 2, 0, df[[varname]]))
  return(df)
}

binary_vars <- c(
  "gender", "smoking_history", "copd_history", "emphysema_ct", "copd_exacerbation",
  "positive_d_dimer", "covid", "elevated_bnp", "elevated_troponin",
  "dvt_in_lower_extremity", "rvsp_based_age", "rv_hypokines_on_echo",
  "pulmonary_hypertension", "rh_thrombus", "rh_strain", "rv_lv_abnormality",
  "tricuspid_regurgitation", "rv_edd_abnormality", "septal_bowing", 
  "clinical_symptoms_dvt", "pe_more_likely", "heart_rate_100", 
  "immobilization_surgery", "dvt_pe", "haemoptysis", "malignancy",   
  "surgery_fracture", "active_malignancy", "unilateral_lower_limb_pain", 
  "pain_lower_limb_edema", "acute_resp"
)

for (var in binary_vars) {
  cases <- clean_binary_variable(cases, var)
}

for (var in binary_vars) {
  controls <- clean_binary_variable(controls, var)
}
```

### Censored Numeric Values

Several numeric variables (`d_dimer_value`, `bnp_levels`, `troponin_levels`, `troponin_levels_hs`, and `map_value`) contained entries reported with inequality symbols (Ex: `<0.015`). For interpretation consistency, all these entries were parsed to retain only their numeric component. For instance, a reported value of `<0.015` was converted to `0.015`, ensuring that the data could be treated as continuous variables for analysis.  

```{r}
numeric_vars <- c("d_dimer_value", "bnp_levels", "troponin_levels", "troponin_levels_hs") 

cases[numeric_vars] <- lapply(cases[numeric_vars], parse_number)
controls[numeric_vars] <- lapply(controls[numeric_vars], parse_number)

cases$map_value <- parse_number(trimws(cases$map_value))
controls$map_value <- parse_number(trimws(controls$map_value))
```


### Variable Type Conversion

To ensure the dataset was compatible with modeling functions, each variable was explicitly converted to its appropriate data type:

  - **Continuous variables** (ex: `age`, `bmi`, `d_dimer_value`, `bnp_levels`, `well_score`) were converted to numeric types.  
  - **Categorical variables**, including all binary indicators and multi-level factors (ex: `gender`, `race`, `smoking_history`, `heart_rate_geneva`), were converted to factor types with clearly defined levels.    
  - **Date or year variables** (ex: `admission_year`) were treated as factors to maintain grouping integrity during stratified analysis.  

```{r}
convert_variables <- function(df) {
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(
      pe_status = factor(pe_status), 
      age = as.numeric(age),
      gender = factor(gender), 
      race = factor(race), 
      bmi = as.numeric(bmi),
      bmi_marker = as.factor(bmi_marker), 

      smoking_history = factor(smoking_history),
      copd_history = factor(copd_history),
      emphysema_ct = factor(emphysema_ct),
      copd_exacerbation = factor(copd_exacerbation), 
      
      positive_d_dimer = factor(positive_d_dimer),
      d_dimer_value = as.numeric(d_dimer_value),
      
      covid = factor(covid),
      elevated_bnp = factor(elevated_bnp),
      bnp_levels = as.numeric(bnp_levels),
      elevated_troponin = factor(elevated_troponin),
      troponin_levels = as.numeric(troponin_levels),
      troponin_levels_hs = as.numeric(troponin_levels_hs),
      dvt_in_lower_extremity = factor(dvt_in_lower_extremity),
    
      rvsp_based_age = factor(rvsp_based_age),
      echo_rvsp_value = as.numeric(echo_rvsp_value),
      rv_hypokines_on_echo = factor(rv_hypokines_on_echo),
      pulmonary_hypertension = factor(pulmonary_hypertension),
      rh_thrombus = factor(rh_thrombus),
      rh_strain = factor(rh_strain),
      rv_to_lv_ratio = as.numeric(rv_to_lv_ratio),
      rv_lv_abnormality = factor(rv_lv_abnormality),
      
      tricuspid_regurgitation = factor(tricuspid_regurgitation),
      rv_edd_cm = as.numeric(rv_edd_cm),
      rv_edd_abnormality = factor(rv_edd_abnormality),
      septal_bowing = factor(septal_bowing),

      clinical_symptoms_dvt = factor(clinical_symptoms_dvt),
      pe_more_likely = factor(pe_more_likely),
      heart_rate_100 = factor(heart_rate_100),
      heart_rate = as.numeric(heart_rate),
      immobilization_surgery = factor(immobilization_surgery),
      dvt_pe = factor(dvt_pe),
      haemoptysis  = factor(haemoptysis),
      malignancy = factor(malignancy),

      surgery_fracture = factor(surgery_fracture),
      active_malignancy = factor(active_malignancy),
      unilateral_lower_limb_pain = factor(unilateral_lower_limb_pain),
      pain_lower_limb_edema = factor(pain_lower_limb_edema), 
      heart_rate_geneva = factor(heart_rate_geneva),
      
      well_score = as.numeric(well_score), 
      revised_geneva_score = as.numeric(revised_geneva_score), 
      admission_year = factor(admission_year), 
      map_value = as.numeric(map_value), 
      acute_resp = factor(acute_resp),
      diastolic = as.numeric(diastolic),
      systolic = as.numeric(systolic), 
      age_group = as.factor(age_group)
  
    )
  
  return(df)
}

cases <- convert_variables(cases)
controls <- convert_variables(controls)
```

```{r}
cases <- cases %>% select(-troponin_levels, -troponin_levels_hs)
controls <- controls %>% select(-troponin_levels, -troponin_levels_hs)
```

### Merging the Case and Control Cohorts

Following preprocessing, the case and control datasets were combined into a single dataset named `merged_data`, comprising **366 observations** and **50 variables**. 

The binary outcome variable, `pe_status`, encodes group membership where:    
- `1` indicates PE-positive (case). 
- `0` indicates PE-negative (control).

Note: To avoid redundancy, the continuous variables `troponin_levels` and `troponin_levels_hs` were excluded after parsing, as they were no longer needed following derivation of its binary variable, `elevated_troponin`

```{r}
merged_data <- bind_rows(cases, controls) 
```

```{r}
str(merged_data)
```


# Part B: Assessment and Handling of Missing Values

To evaluate data completeness, a summary was generated across all variables to calculate the percentage of missing values. This helps inform the choice between imputation and complete case analysis. 

Each variable was categorized based on the extent of missingness:

- **<5% Missing**: Minimal impact (fit for imputation or modeling with minimal concern). 
- **5–20% Missing**: Moderate concern (may require targeted imputation or sensitivity analysis).  
- **>20% Missing**: High concern (consideration for exclusion).   

These summaries of missingness for each variable are displayed below in three separate tables: 

```{r}
missing_summary <- merged_data %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~mean(is.na(.)) * 100)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Percent_Missing") %>%
  filter(Percent_Missing > 0) %>%
  mutate(Category = case_when(
    Percent_Missing < 5 ~ "<5% Missing",
    Percent_Missing >= 5 & Percent_Missing <= 20 ~ "5–20% Missing",
    Percent_Missing > 20 ~ ">20% Missing"
  )) %>%
  arrange(desc(Percent_Missing))

minimal_missing <- missing_summary %>% filter(Category == "<5% Missing")
moderate_missing <- missing_summary %>% filter(Category == "5–20% Missing")
high_missing <- missing_summary %>% filter(Category == ">20% Missing")


minimal_missing %>%
  select(Variable, Percent_Missing) %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Less than 5% Missing") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))

moderate_missing %>%
  select(Variable, Percent_Missing) %>%
  kable("html", caption = "5–20% Missing") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))

high_missing %>%
  select(Variable, Percent_Missing) %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Greater than 20% Missing") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```

## Handling Missingess of Variables with <5% Missing Data  

For variables with less than 5% missingness, the mechanism of missing data was evaluated to determine whether it could be classified as **Missing Completely at Random (MCAR)**. MCAR refers to missing data where the probability of missingness is unrelated to both observed and unobserved variables.

To assess this, **Little’s MCAR test** was applied, which uses a chi-squared statistic to compare means and covariances across patterns of missingness. The test returned:

- **χ² = 21.97**,  
- **df = 33**,  
- **p-value = 0.928**.

Given the high p-value, the null hypothesis could not be rejected, indicating no significant difference between complete and incomplete cases. This supports the assumption that the data are MCAR, meaning the missingness appears to be random and not associated with either the outcome variable (`pe_status`) or other covariates.

To further support this conclusion, **Fisher’s Exact Test** was used to assess the association between missingness in the selected predictors and the outcome variable. The test yielded a **p-value = 0.3221**, providing additional evidence that the missingness is independent of pulmonary embolism status and consistent with the MCAR assumption.

```{r}
vars_under_5 <- c("smoking_history", "emphysema_ct", "copd_history", "copd_exacerbation", 
                  "clinical_symptoms_dvt", "immobilization_surgery", "dvt_pe", 
                  "haemoptysis", "malignancy", "surgery_fracture", "active_malignancy", 
                  "unilateral_lower_limb_pain", "pain_lower_limb_edema", "well_score", 
                  "revised_geneva_score", "pe_more_likely")

data_subset<- merged_data[, vars_under_5]
mcar_test(data_subset)
```

```{r}
merged_data$any_missing_subset <- apply(is.na(data_subset), 1, any)
fisher.test(table(merged_data$any_missing_subset, merged_data$pe_status))
```

```{r}
merged_data <- merged_data %>%
  select(-c(any_missing_subset))
```

Given that the missingness was determined to be **Missing Completely at Random (MCAR)** and affects less than 5% of observations for each variable, either simple imputation or complete case analysis can be applied without introducing systematic bias. To proceed conservatively, a complete case analysis was conducted by removing all rows with missing values for the selected subset of variables. This process excluded **9 observations**, representing only **2.46%** of the dataset. The resulting dataset retained approximately **97.5%** of the original sample, minimizing the risk of reduced statistical power or biased inference due to data loss.

```{r}
n_complete <- sum(complete.cases(data_subset))
n_total <- nrow(data_subset)
n_dropped <- n_total - n_complete

cat("Number of rows that would be dropped:", n_dropped, "\n")
cat("Percentage of data dropped:", round((n_dropped / n_total) * 100, 2), "%\n")
```

Sensitivity Analysis: To assess the robustness of the missing data handling strategy, a sensitivity analysis was performed by comparing results from complete case analysis with those obtained through simple imputation.

In the imputation approach:  
- Missing values in **categorical variables** were replaced with the model.  
- Missing values in **numerical variables** were imputed using the mean of the respective variable.    

Logistic regression models were fit to both the complete case and imputed datasets to predict the binary outcome variable `pe_status`. Model fit was compared using the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC):

- **Complete Case Model**: AIC = **348.98**  
- **Imputed Data Model**: AIC = **353.70**

The slightly lower AIC in the complete case model suggests a marginally better fit. In this comparison, the complete case approach was selected for the final analysis. This resulted in the exclusion of **9 rows**, retaining a total of **357 observations**, and preserving 97.5% of the original dataset.

```{r}
data_complete_case <- na.omit(data_subset) 
get_mode <- function(x) {
  ux <- unique(x[!is.na(x)])
  ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]
}

data_imputed <- data_subset %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ ifelse(is.na(.), mean(., na.rm = TRUE), .))) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.factor), ~ ifelse(is.na(.), get_mode(.), .)))

data_complete_case$pe_status <- merged_data$pe_status[complete.cases(data_subset)]
data_imputed$pe_status <- merged_data$pe_status

model_cc <- glm(pe_status ~ ., data = data_complete_case, family = binomial)
model_imp <- glm(pe_status ~ ., data = data_imputed, family = binomial)

aic_values <- data.frame(
  Method = c("Complete Case Analysis", "Simple Imputation"),
  AIC = c(AIC(model_cc), AIC(model_imp))
)

aic_values %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Comparison of AIC Values: Complete Case vs Imputation") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))

merged_data <- merged_data[complete.cases(merged_data[, vars_under_5]), ]
```


## Handling Missingess of Variables with 5-20 percent missingness 

The only variable with **moderate missingness** (between 5% and 20%) is `elevated_troponin`, with 7.37% of values missing. To assess the nature of this missingness, its relationship with the outcome variable `pe_status` (pulmonary embolism diagnosis) was examined.

A cross-tabulation showed that among individuals diagnosed with PE, 170 had observed `elevated_troponin` values and 17 had missing values. In contrast, among individuals without PE, 161 had observed values and 9 had missing values. 

To further assess any potential impact of missingness, the PE diagnosis rate was calculated separately for those with and without observed troponin values. The PE rate was:

- **48.6%** among those with observed troponin values  
- **34.6%** among those with missing troponin values

The different proportions of missingness across the two groups suggest that missingness is to be systematically associated with PE status, supporting the assumption that the data may not be **Missing Completely at Random (MCAR)**.

```{r}
troponin_pe_table <- table(is.na(merged_data$elevated_troponin), merged_data$pe_status)

troponin_pe_df <- as.data.frame.matrix(troponin_pe_table)
rownames(troponin_pe_df) <- c("Observed (Not Missing)", "Missing")
troponin_pe_df <- tibble::rownames_to_column(troponin_pe_df, var = "Troponin Missingness")
colnames(troponin_pe_df)[2:3] <- c("PE Absent (0)", "PE Present (1)")

troponin_pe_df %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Cross-tabulation of Troponin Missingness by PE Status") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r}
merged_data %>%
  mutate(pe_status_num = as.numeric(as.character(pe_status)),
         troponin_missing = ifelse(is.na(elevated_troponin), "Missing", "Not Missing")) %>%
  group_by(troponin_missing) %>%
  summarise(pe_rate = mean(pe_status_num, na.rm = TRUE),
            n = n()) %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Pulmonary Embolism Rate by Elevated Troponin Missingness") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```

Although this difference appears notable, statistical testing was conducted to evaluate its significance. Two statistical tests were performed:

- **Chi-square test of independence**:  
  - χ² = 1.38, df = 1, **p-value = 0.24**  
  - No significant association between missingness and PE status.

- **Little’s MCAR test**:  
  - χ² = 1.90, df = 1, **p-value = 0.168**  
  - Supports the assumption that missingness in `elevated_troponin` is consistent with MCAR.


```{r}
chisq.test(table(is.na(merged_data$elevated_troponin), merged_data$pe_status))
mcar_test(merged_data[,c("elevated_troponin","pe_status")]) 
```

Although statistical tests supported the assumption that missing values in `elevated_troponin` were **Missing Completely at Random (MCAR)**, the observed differences in missingness proportions between cases and controls suggest that relying solely on complete case analysis may not be appropriate. Additionally, applying complete case analysis would have excluded 26 observations, which could introduce bias if missingness is even weakly related to other variables. To address this, imputation was conducted under the more flexible **Missing At Random (MAR)** assumption using **Multiple Imputation by Chained Equations (MICE)**.

To identify a robust set of covariates for the imputation model, all variables with **no missing values** were extracted from the dataset and a **Random Forest classifier** was trained on the complete cases of `elevated_troponin` using these variables to predict its presence or absence. The 10 variables to be considered including in the imputation model were ranked by **Mean Decrease in Accuracy**, a measure of their predictive importance.

```{r}
no_missing_vars <- names(merged_data)[colSums(is.na(merged_data)) == 0]
merged_data_no_missing <- merged_data[, no_missing_vars]
```

```{r}
formula_str <- paste(
  "elevated_troponin ~", 
  paste(no_missing_vars[no_missing_vars != "elevated_troponin"], collapse = " + ")
)
rf_formula <- as.formula(formula_str)

rf_data <- merged_data %>% filter(!is.na(elevated_troponin))

set.seed(123)
rf_model <- randomForest(
  formula = rf_formula,
  data = rf_data,
  importance = TRUE, 
  ntree = 500
)

var_importance <- importance(rf_model, type = 1) 
top_vars <- rownames(var_importance)[order(-var_importance[, 1])][1:10]

importance_df <- as.data.frame(importance(rf_model))
importance_df$Variable <- rownames(importance_df)

top10_vars <- importance_df %>%
  arrange(desc(MeanDecreaseAccuracy)) %>%
  select(Variable, MeanDecreaseAccuracy) %>%
  slice(1:10)

top10_vars %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Top 10 Predictors of Elevated Troponin (by Mean Decrease Accuracy)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

To ensure accurate imputation of the `elevated_troponin` variable, an automated procedure was used to identify the optimal subset of predictors from the top 10 predictors above: 

- `bmi`, `acute_resp`, `bmi_marker`, `map_value`, `heart_rate`,  
  `well_score`, `heart_rate_100`, `diastolic`,  
  `unilateral_lower_limb_pain`, `active_malignancy`

All combinations of 3 to 6 predictors were evaluated using the following steps:

1. **Imputation**: Logistic regression-based imputation via `mice` (5 imputations, 10 iterations). 
2. **Distribution Check**: Compared class proportions (0 vs. 1) between observed and imputed values.
3. **Model Stability**: Fit logistic models predicting `pe_status` using both complete and imputed data. 
4. **Scoring**: A composite score was computed based on differences in:
   - Class proportions  
   - Regression coefficients for `elevated_troponin`  
   - Associated p-values

Combinations of predictors with the lowest scores were preferred and were considered in including in the imputation model. 

```{#my-long-running-code-block .r eval="false"}
top_predictors <- c("bmi", "acute_resp", "bmi_marker", "map_value", "heart_rate", 
                    "well_score", "heart_rate_100", "diastolic", 
                    "unilateral_lower_limb_pain", "active_malignancy")

outcome <- "elevated_troponin"

evaluate_combo <- function(predictors) {
  impute_vars <- c(outcome, "pe_status", predictors)
  impute_data <- merged_data[, impute_vars]

  imp <- tryCatch({
    mice(impute_data, method = "logreg", m = 5, maxit = 10, seed = 123, print = FALSE)
  }, error = function(e) return(NULL))
  if (is.null(imp)) return(NULL)

  complete_data <- complete(imp, 1)
  temp_data <- merged_data
  temp_data$imputed_tr <- complete_data[[outcome]]

  mask_obs <- !is.na(impute_data[[outcome]])
  observed <- temp_data[mask_obs, outcome, drop = TRUE]
  imputed <- temp_data[!mask_obs, "imputed_tr", drop = TRUE]

  prop_obs_1 <- mean(observed == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  prop_obs_0 <- mean(observed == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  prop_imp_1 <- mean(imputed == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  prop_imp_0 <- mean(imputed == 0, na.rm = TRUE)

  prop_diff_1 <- abs(prop_obs_1 - prop_imp_1)
  prop_diff_0 <- abs(prop_obs_0 - prop_imp_0)

  model_complete <- tryCatch({
    glm(pe_status ~ get(outcome),
        data = temp_data[mask_obs, ],
        family = binomial)
  }, error = function(e) return(NULL))

  model_imputed <- tryCatch({
    glm(pe_status ~ imputed_tr,
        data = temp_data,
        family = binomial)
  }, error = function(e) return(NULL))

  if (is.null(model_complete) || is.null(model_imputed)) return(NULL)

  coef_complete <- tryCatch(coef(model_complete)[2], error = function(e) NA)
  coef_imputed <- tryCatch(coef(model_imputed)[2], error = function(e) NA)
  pval_complete <- tryCatch(summary(model_complete)$coefficients[2, 4], error = function(e) NA)
  pval_imputed <- tryCatch(summary(model_imputed)$coefficients[2, 4], error = function(e) NA)

  coef_diff <- abs(coef_complete - coef_imputed)
  pval_diff <- abs(pval_complete - pval_imputed)

  score <- prop_diff_1 + prop_diff_0 + coef_diff + pval_diff

  return(tibble(
    predictors = paste(predictors, collapse = ", "),
    prop_diff_1 = round(prop_diff_1, 3),
    prop_diff_0 = round(prop_diff_0, 3),
    coef_diff = round(coef_diff, 3),
    pval_diff = round(pval_diff, 3),
    score = round(score, 3)
  ))
}

combinations <- unlist(lapply(3:6, function(n) combn(top_predictors, n, simplify = FALSE)), recursive = FALSE)
safe_results <- map(combinations, safely(evaluate_combo))
successful_results <- keep(safe_results, ~ is.null(.x$error))
results <- map_dfr(successful_results, ~ as_tibble(.x$result)) %>%
  arrange(score)

print(head(results, 10))
```


The best-performing combination, based on the composite score, included:

- `pe_status`, `elevated_troponin`, `bmi`, `acute_resp`, `bmi_marker`, `map_value`, `well_score`

This set was used in the final imputation step using logistic regression within the `mice` framework (5 imputations, 10 iterations). The first completed dataset was selected, and imputed values for the elevated_troponin variable were inserted directly into the original `merged_data` dataset. 

```{r}
impute_vars <- c("pe_status", "elevated_troponin", "bmi", "acute_resp", "bmi_marker", "map_value", "well_score") 
impute_data <- merged_data[, impute_vars]
```

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}
capture.output({
  imputed_data <- mice(
    impute_data,
    m = 5,
    method = "logreg",
    maxit = 10,
    seed = 123
  )
}, file = NULL)
```

```{r}
pre_imputation_data <- merged_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(elevated_troponin))
```

```{r}
completed_data <- complete(imputed_data, 1)
merged_data$elevated_troponin[is.na(merged_data$elevated_troponin)] <- 
  completed_data$elevated_troponin[is.na(merged_data$elevated_troponin)]
```


**Sensitivity Analysis: Validating Imputation of Elevated Troponin ** 

**Distributional Consistency:** To validate the robustness of the imputation strategy, a sensitivity analysis was conducted to evaluate whether imputing missing values for `elevated_troponin` preserved the integrity of the dataset. A bar plot comparing the proportions of `elevated_troponin` values (0 vs. 1) between observed and imputed cases revealed closely aligned distributions. This suggests that the imputation procedure maintained the original variable structure and did not distort class proportions.

```{r}
merged_data %>%
  mutate(trop_flag = ifelse(is.na(impute_data$elevated_troponin), "Imputed", "Observed")) %>%
  group_by(trop_flag, elevated_troponin) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(trop_flag) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(elevated_troponin), y = prop, fill = trop_flag)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  labs(title = "Proportion of Elevated Troponin (Observed vs Imputed)",
       x = "Elevated Troponin", y = "Proportion") +
  theme_minimal()
```


**Impact on Model Estimates: ** To assess whether imputation affected inferential conclusions of predicting pe_status, two logistic regression models were fitted to predict `pe_status`:

- **Pre-imputation model**: Using only complete cases (observed elevated_troponin values)
- **Post-imputation model**: Using the full dataset with imputed values of elevated_troponin

Both models included the same predictor set used in the imputation model and the results showcased: 

- The coefficient for `elevated_troponin_1` shifted minimally from **-0.143** (pre-imputation) to **-0.157** (post-imputation).
- `elevated_troponin` remained **non-significant** in both models.

These results confirm that the imputation procedure did not introduce bias or significantly alter variable relationships. Therefore, the multiple imputation approach was appropriate for the elevated_troponin variable. 

```{r}
impute_vars <- c("elevated_troponin", "bmi", "acute_resp", "bmi_marker", "map_value", "well_score") 
logit_formula <- as.formula(paste("pe_status ~", paste(impute_vars, collapse = " + ")))

model_complete <- glm(logit_formula,
                      data = pre_imputation_data,
                      family = binomial)

model_imputed <- glm(logit_formula,
                     data = merged_data,
                     family = binomial)

summary_complete <- summary(model_complete)
summary_imputed <- summary(model_imputed)

logit_table <- data.frame(
  Coef_Complete = round(summary_complete$coefficients[, "Estimate"], 3),
  P_Complete = round(summary_complete$coefficients[, "Pr(>|z|)"], 3),
  Coef_Imputed = round(summary_imputed$coefficients[, "Estimate"], 3),
  P_Imputed = round(summary_imputed$coefficients[, "Pr(>|z|)"], 3)
)


logit_table_sorted <- logit_table[order(logit_table$P_Imputed), ]

logit_table_sorted %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Logistic Regression Comparison Between Pre and Post Imputated Data") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)

```


## Handling Missingness of Variables with more than 20 percent missingness 

Four variables (`rv_to_lv_ratio`, `rv_lv_abnormality`, `rv_edd_cm`, and `rv_edd_abnormality`) had more than 80% missing values. When missingness exceeds this threshold, both simple and advanced imputation methods become unreliable and can introduce substantial bias into the analysis. Therefore, these variables were excluded from the dataset. After removing these variables, the dataset has a total of 46 variables for subsequent analysis.

```{r}
merged_data <- merged_data %>%
  select(-c(rv_to_lv_ratio, rv_lv_abnormality, rv_edd_cm, rv_edd_abnormality))
```


### Handling Missingness of positive_d_dimer and d_dimer_value

The variable `d_dimer_value`, which is a continuous measure of a blood clot degradation product exhibited **24.86% missingness**, identical to its binary counterpart `positive_d_dimer`.

A cross-tabulation showed the distribution of missingness by pulmonary embolism (PE) status:

- Among individuals **with PE**, 139 had observed `d_dimer_value` and 48 had missing entries.
- Among individuals **without PE**, 130 had observed values and 40 had missing.

The similar proportions of missingness across the two groups suggest that the missingness is not strongly associated with PE status, supporting the assumption that the missingness of the `d_dimer_value` variable may be **Missing Completely at Random (MCAR)**. 

```{r}
d_dimer_pe_table <- table(is.na(merged_data$d_dimer_value), merged_data$pe_status)
d_dimer_pe_df <- as.data.frame.matrix(d_dimer_pe_table)
rownames(d_dimer_pe_df) <- c("Observed (Not Missing)", "Missing")
d_dimer_pe_df <- tibble::rownames_to_column(d_dimer_pe_df, var = "d-Dimer Levels Missingness")
colnames(d_dimer_pe_df)[2:3] <- c("PE Absent (0)", "PE Present (1)")
d_dimer_pe_df %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Cross-tabulation of d-Dimer Levels Missingness by PE Status") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

Furthermore, the conclusion that the missingness is MCAR is supported by running two statistical tests:   
- **Chi-square test of independence** yielded a non-significant p-value of **0.7298**, indicating no association between missingness and PE status.   
- **Little’s MCAR test** returned a p-value of **0.640**, further supporting the MCAR assumption.  

```{r}
chisq.test(table(is.na(merged_data$d_dimer_value), merged_data$pe_status))
mcar_test(merged_data[,c("d_dimer_value","pe_status")]) 
```

**Logistic Regression Analysis of Missingness**

To further examine the mechanism behind the missing data, a logistic regression model was used to predict the binary indicator `missing_d_dimer_value` (1 = missing, 0 = observed), using only variables with complete data to avoid additional bias.

The results showed:  
- **`pe_status` was not a significant predictor** of missingness.    
- However, **`well_score` and `admission_year`** were significantly associated with missing values in `d_dimer_value`.  

This pattern suggests that although the missingness may appear random with respect to the outcome variable, it is influenced by other observed variables, consistent with the **Missing At Random (MAR)** mechanism.

Given these findings, **multiple imputation** was chosen over complete case analysis to preserve statistical power and reduce potential bias.

```{r}
merged_data$missing_d_dimer_value<- as.numeric(is.na(merged_data$d_dimer_value))
```

```{r}
no_missing_vars <- names(merged_data)[colSums(is.na(merged_data)) == 0]
merged_data_no_missing <- merged_data[, no_missing_vars]
```

```{r}
excluded_vars <- c("d_dimer_value", "missing_d_dimer_value", "positive_d_dimer")
predictor_vars <- setdiff(names(merged_data_no_missing), excluded_vars)

formula_str <- paste("missing_d_dimer_value ~", paste(predictor_vars, collapse = " + "))
formula <- as.formula(formula_str)

missingness_model <- glm(formula, data = merged_data_no_missing, family = binomial)

significant_vars <- tidy(missingness_model) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)", p.value < 0.1) %>%
  arrange(p.value)

significant_vars %>%
  mutate(p.value = signif(p.value, 3)) %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Significant Predictors of Missingness in d-dimer values") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

**Imputation of d_dimer_value: ** 

Missing values in `d_dimer_value` were imputed using **Predictive Mean Matching (PMM)** implemented via the `mice` package. To accommodate the skewed distribution of `d_dimer_value`, the variable was first log-transformed using `log1p()`. The imputation was performed over **5 datasets with 10 iterations each**, using the following predictors:

- Variables identified as significantly associated with missingness:  
  `well_score`, `admission_year`, and others (see table above).  
- Additional clinically and statistically relevant variables:    
  `age`, `gender`, `race`, `revised_geneva_score`, `pe_status`, `heart_rate_geneva`, `pe_more_likely`.  

A predictor matrix was used to limit predictors to this predefined set. After imputation, the log-transformed values were back-transformed using `expm1()` to return to the original scale.

Finally, the binary variable `positive_d_dimer` was recalculated from the imputed values, where values > 0.5 µg/mL were coded as 1 (positive), and ≤ 0.5 µg/mL as 0 (negative).

```{r}
mandatory_predictors <- c(
  "age", "well_score", "race", "pe_more_likely", "admission_year", "gender", "revised_geneva_score", "pe_status", "heart_rate_geneva"
)

impute_predictors <- c(mandatory_predictors) 
```

```{r}
merged_data$log_d_dimer <- log1p(merged_data$d_dimer_value)
impute_data <- merged_data[, c("log_d_dimer", impute_predictors)]
```

```{r}
pred_matrix <- make.predictorMatrix(impute_data)
pred_matrix[,] <- 0 
pred_matrix["log_d_dimer", impute_predictors] <- 1
```

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}
capture.output(
  imp <- mice(impute_data,
              method = "pmm", 
              predictorMatrix = pred_matrix,
              m = 5, 
              maxit = 10,
              seed = 123),
  file = NULL
)
```

```{r}
log_d_dimer_imputed <- complete(imp, 1)$log_d_dimer
merged_data$d_dimer_value <- expm1(log_d_dimer_imputed)
```

```{r}
merged_data$d_dimer_value <- as.numeric(merged_data$d_dimer_value)
merged_data$positive_d_dimer <- factor(
  ifelse(merged_data$d_dimer_value > 0.5, 1, 0),
  levels = c(0, 1)
)
```

**Validation of Imputed d_dimer_value and derived positive_d_dimer ** 

The imputation of `d_dimer_value` was evaluated by comparing distributions between observed and imputed values. Summary statistics show similar central tendencies across groups: the **mean** values were 5.20 (observed) and 5.45 (imputed), and **median** values were 1.88 and 1.79, respectively.

Statistical comparisons confirmed these similarities:  
- **Welch Two-Sample t-test**: *p* = 0.8083   
- **Wilcoxon Rank-Sum test**: *p* = 0.9218    

Both p-values exceed 0.05, indicating no significant difference in means or distributions between the groups.

This conclusion is further supported by a **density plot**, which shows substantial overlap between observed and imputed distributions with no apparent shift. Together, these findings indicate that the imputation procedure effectively preserved the original data structure of the d-dimer values and did not introduce systematic bias.

```{r}
imputed_df <- complete(imp, 1)
imputed_df$imputed_flag <- ifelse(is.na(merged_data$log_d_dimer), "Imputed", "Observed")

imputed_df$d_dimer_value <- expm1(imputed_df$log_d_dimer)

summary_table <- imputed_df %>%
  mutate(imputed_flag = factor(imputed_flag, levels = c("Observed", "Imputed"))) %>%
  group_by(imputed_flag) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean = round(mean(d_dimer_value, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    Median = round(median(d_dimer_value, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    SD = round(sd(d_dimer_value, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    N = n(),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

summary_table %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Summary of d-dimer by Imputation Status") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"))
```

```{r}
t.test(d_dimer_value ~ imputed_flag, data = imputed_df)
wilcox.test(d_dimer_value ~ imputed_flag, data = imputed_df)
```

```{r}
ggplot(imputed_df, aes(x = d_dimer_value, fill = imputed_flag)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Observed vs. Imputed d-dimer Levels",
    x = "BNP Levels",
    y = "Density",
    fill = "Value Type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
merged_data <- merged_data %>% select(-missing_d_dimer_value)
```


### Handling Missingness of bnp_levels and elevated_bnp

Missingness in `bnp_levels` (28.4%) and its binary counterpart `elevated_bnp` (27.6%) was evaluated similarly to `d_dimer_value`. Among PE cases, 134 had observed values and 53 were missing; among controls, 123 had observed values and 47 were missing. This balanced distribution indicates that there is possibly no association between missingness in this variable and PE status.

```{r}
bnp_pe_table <- table(is.na(merged_data$bnp_levels), merged_data$pe_status)
bnp_pe_df <- as.data.frame.matrix(bnp_pe_table)

  kable("html", caption = "Cross-tabulation of BNP Levels Missingness by PE Status") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

Two statistical tests were conducted to further support the MCAR assumption of the missingnes in `bnp_levels`:   
- **Chi-square test**: *p* = 0.9776  
- **Little’s MCAR test**: *p* = 0.884  

Both results support the assumption that missingness in BNP-related variables is **Missing Completely at Random (MCAR)**.

```{r}
chisq.test(table(is.na(merged_data$bnp_levels), merged_data$pe_status))
mcar_test(merged_data[,c("bnp_levels","pe_status")]) 
```

**Logistic Regression Analysis of Missingness ** 

To investigate the mechanism behind missing values in `bnp_levels`, a logistic regression was conducted to evaluate whether missingness was associated with other observed variables. A binary indicator variable `missing_bnp_levels` was created, coded as 1 for missing values and 0 for observed ones.

To prevent bias and row exclusion due to missing data, the analysis was limited to variables with complete data. The logistic regression results showed that `pe_status` was not a significant predictor of missingness. However, variables such as `copd_history1` and `admission_year2020` weakly predicted missingness in `bnp_levels`.

These findings suggest that although the data are largely consistent with the **Missing Completely at Random (MCAR)** assumption, there is slight dependence on observed variables, aligning better with the **Missing at Random (MAR)** framework. Consequently, multiple imputation was selected over complete case analysis to retain statistical power and minimize bias.

```{r}
merged_data$missing_bnp_levels<- as.numeric(is.na(merged_data$bnp_levels))
```


```{r}

predictor_vars <- setdiff(names(merged_data_no_missing), excluded_vars)

  filter(term != "(Intercept)", p.value < 0.1) %>%

significant_vars %>%
  mutate(p.value = signif(p.value, 3)) %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Significant Predictors of Missingness in bnp_levels") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

**Imputation of bnp_levels: ** 

Missing values in `bnp_levels` were imputed using Predictive Mean Matching (PMM) via the MICE algorithm. Predictor variables included:  
1. Variables significantly associated with missingness (identified via logistic regression), and  
2. Clinically relevant predictors related to both `pe_status` and BNP (B-type natrieretic peptide), a biomarker for heart strain and failure, such as `heart_rate`, `systolic`, `diastolic`, and `age`.

To accommodate the right-skewed distribution of BNP, `bnp_levels` was log-transformed using `log1p()` before imputation. The MICE procedure was run with 5 imputations and 10 iterations. After imputation, values were back-transformed using `expm1()` to restore the original scale.

A binary variable, `elevated_bnp`, was derived from the imputed values, with values >100 pg/mL coded as 1 and others as 0.

### Handling Missingness of covid

The variable `covid` has 31.96% missing data. To evaluate whether this missingness is related to the outcome variable `pe_status`, a cross-tabulation was performed. Among PE cases, 127 had observed `covid` values and 60 were missing; among non-PE individuals, 115 had observed values and 55 were missing. The proportion of missingness is comparable between the two groups, suggesting that missingness is likely not systematically associated with PE diagnosis.

To further investigate, the PE rate was compared between those with observed and missing `covid` data. The PE rate was 47.5% in the observed group and 47.8% in the missing group, showing negligible difference. These patterns support the assumption that the missingness in `covid` is consistent with a **Missing Completely At Random (MCAR)** mechanism.

```{r}
covid_pe_table <- table(is.na(merged_data$covid), merged_data$pe_status)

covid_pe_df <- as.data.frame.matrix(covid_pe_table)
rownames(covid_pe_df) <- c("Observed (Not Missing)", "Missing")
covid_pe_df <- tibble::rownames_to_column(covid_pe_df, var = "COVID Missingness")
colnames(covid_pe_df)[2:3] <- c("PE Absent (0)", "PE Present (1)")

covid_pe_df %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Cross-tabulation of COVID Missingness by PE Status") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r}
merged_data %>%
  mutate(pe_status_num = as.numeric(as.character(pe_status)),
         covid_missing = ifelse(is.na(covid), "Missing", "Not Missing")) %>%
  group_by(covid_missing) %>%
  summarise(pe_rate = mean(pe_status_num, na.rm = TRUE),
            n = n()) %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Pulmonary Embolism Rate by COVID Missingness") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```

While diagnostic tests suggest that missingness in the `covid` variable is consistent with a **Missing Completely At Random (MCAR)** mechanism, a less conservative **Missing At Random (MAR)** framework is used to execute imputation of the missing values. This decision avoids the loss of 115 observations that would occur with complete case analysis, thereby preserving statistical power and minimizing potential bias, particularly if missingness is weakly linked to the outcome variable `pe_status`.

To identify a robust set of covariates for the imputation model, all variables with **no missing values** were extracted from the dataset and a **Random Forest classifier** was trained on the complete cases of `covid` using these variables to predict its presence or absence. The 10 variables to be considered including in the imputation model were ranked by **Mean Decrease in Accuracy**, a measure of their predictive importance.

```{r}
no_missing_vars <- names(merged_data)[colSums(is.na(merged_data)) == 0]
merged_data_no_missing <- merged_data[, no_missing_vars]
```

```{r}
formula_str <- paste(
  "covid ~", 
  paste(no_missing_vars[no_missing_vars != "covid"], collapse = " + ")
)
rf_formula <- as.formula(formula_str)

rf_data <- merged_data %>% filter(!is.na(covid))

set.seed(123)
rf_model <- randomForest(
  formula = rf_formula,
  data = rf_data,
  importance = TRUE, 
  ntree = 500
)

var_importance <- importance(rf_model, type = 1)

  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

To impute missing values in `covid`, we applied the same iterative approach used for previous variables, utilizing **Multiple Imputation by Chained Equations (MICE)** with logistic regression. The imputation model included `pe_status` and a targeted set of predictors identified via Random Forest variable importance on complete cases. The selected covariates (`map_value`, `diastolic`, `heart_rate`, `age`, and `elevated_troponin`) demonstrated strong predictive value and had no missingness themselves. 


The imputation process was performed across 5 datasets with 10 iterations each. The first completed dataset was used to fill in the missing `covid` values, ensuring consistency with observed data patterns and preserving relationships with key clinical variables.

```{r}
impute_vars <- c("pe_status", "covid", "map_value", "diastolic", "heart_rate", "age", "elevated_troponin")
impute_data <- merged_data[, impute_vars]
```

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}
capture.output({
  imputed_data <- mice(
    impute_data,
    m = 5,
    method = "logreg",
    maxit = 10,
    seed = 123
  )
}, file = NULL)
```

```{r}
pre_imputation_data <- merged_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(covid))
```

```{r}
completed_data <- complete(imputed_data, 1)
merged_data$covid[is.na(merged_data$covid)] <- 
  completed_data$covid[is.na(merged_data$covid)]
```

**Sensitivity Analysis: Validating Imputation of covid ** 

**Distributional Consistency:** To validate the robustness of the imputation strategy, a sensitivity analysis was conducted to evaluate whether imputing missing values for `covid` preserved the integrity of the dataset. A bar plot comparing the proportions of `covid` values (0 vs. 1) between observed and imputed cases revealed closely aligned distributions. This suggests that the imputation procedure maintained the original variable structure and did not distort class proportions.

```{r}
merged_data %>%
  mutate(covid_flag = ifelse(is.na(impute_data$covid), "Imputed", "Observed")) %>%
  group_by(covid_flag, covid) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(covid_flag) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(covid), y = prop, fill = covid_flag)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  labs(title = "Proportion of COVID-19 (Observed vs Imputed)",
       x = "COVID - 19", y = "Proportion") +
  theme_minimal()
```


**Impact on Model Estimates: ** We further assessed the effect of imputation on model estimates by fitting logistic regression models predicting `pe_status` before and after imputation. Both models used the same covariates included in the imputation model. Results showed statistically nonsignificant effect of `covid` on PE status in either model: 

- The coefficient for `covid` changed only slightly from **-0.227 ** (pre-imputation) to **-0.131** (imputed), reinforcing that the imputation did not meaningfully alter the relationship between `covid` and the outcome.

```{r}
impute_vars <- c("covid", "map_value", "diastolic", "heart_rate", "age", "elevated_troponin")
logit_formula <- as.formula(paste("pe_status ~", paste(impute_vars, collapse = " + ")))

model_complete <- glm(logit_formula,
                      data = pre_imputation_data,
                      family = binomial)

model_imputed <- glm(logit_formula,
                     data = merged_data,
                     family = binomial)

summary_complete <- summary(model_complete)
summary_imputed <- summary(model_imputed)

logit_table <- data.frame(
  Coef_Complete = round(summary_complete$coefficients[, "Estimate"], 3),
  P_Complete = round(summary_complete$coefficients[, "Pr(>|z|)"], 3),
  Coef_Imputed = round(summary_imputed$coefficients[, "Estimate"], 3),
  P_Imputed = round(summary_imputed$coefficients[, "Pr(>|z|)"], 3)
)


logit_table_sorted <- logit_table[order(logit_table$P_Imputed), ]

logit_table_sorted %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Logistic Regression Comparison Between Pre and Post Imputated Data") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

### Handling Missingness of dvt_in_lower_extremity 

The variable `dvt_in_lower_extremity` has 35.79% missing data. To evaluate whether this missingness is related to the outcome variable `pe_status`, a cross-tabulation was performed. Among PE cases, 83 had observed `dvt_in_lower_extremity` values and 104 were missing; among non-PE individuals, 146 had observed values and 24 were missing. The proportion of missingness is vastly different between the two groups, suggesting that missingness is likely systematically associated with PE diagnosis.

To further investigate, the PE rate was compared between those with observed and missing `dvt_in_lower_extremity` data. The PE rate was 63.75% in the observed group and 18.75% in the missing group, showing notable difference. These patterns support the assumption that the missingness in `dvt_in_lower_extremity` is not consistent with a **Missing Completely At Random (MCAR)** mechanism.

**Sensitivity Analysis: Validating Imputation of septal_bowing ** 

**Distributional Consistency:** To validate the robustness of the imputation strategy, a sensitivity analysis was conducted to evaluate whether imputing missing values for `septal_bowing` preserved the integrity of the dataset. A bar plot comparing the proportions of `septal_bowing` values (0 vs. 1) between observed and imputed cases revealed closely aligned distributions. This suggests that the imputation procedure maintained the original variable structure and did not distort class proportions.

```{r}
merged_data %>%

  group_by(septal_bowing_flag, septal_bowing) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(septal_bowing_flag) %>%

       x = "Septal Bowing", y = "Proportion") +
  theme_minimal()
```

**Impact on Model Estimates: ** We further assessed the effect of imputation on model estimates by fitting logistic regression models predicting `pe_status` before and after imputation. Both models used the same covariates included in the imputation model. Results showed a statistically non significant effect of `septal_bowing` on PE status in either model at the 0.10 significance level: 

- The coefficient for `septal_bowing` changed only slightly from **-1.542 ** (pre-imputation) to **-1.491** (imputed), reinforcing that the imputation did not meaningfully alter the relationship between `septal_bowing` and the outcome.

```{r}
impute_vars <- c("septal_bowing", "revised_geneva_score", "heart_rate", "map_value")

                     data = merged_data,

  Coef_Complete = round(summary_complete$coefficients[, "Estimate"], 3),
  P_Complete = round(summary_complete$coefficients[, "Pr(>|z|)"], 3),
```

### Handling Missingness of rh_strain

The variable `rh_strain` has 39.617% missing data. To evaluate whether this missingness is related to the outcome variable `pe_status`, a cross-tabulation was performed. Among PE cases, 98 had observed `rh_strain` values and 89 were missing; among non-PE individuals, 117 had observed values and 53 were missing. The proportion of missingness is vastly different between the two groups, suggesting that missingness is likely systematically associated with PE diagnosis.

To further investigate, the PE rate was compared between those with observed and missing `rh_strain` data. The PE rate was 54.4% in the observed group and 37.32% in the missing group, showing notable difference. These patterns support the assumption that the missingness in `rh_strain` is not consistent with a **Missing Completely At Random (MCAR)** mechanism.

```{r}
rh_strain_pe_table <- table(is.na(merged_data$rh_strain), merged_data$pe_status)

rh_strain_pe_df <- as.data.frame.matrix(rh_strain_pe_table)
rownames(rh_strain_pe_df) <- c("Observed (Not Missing)", "Missing")
rh_strain_pe_df <- tibble::rownames_to_column(rh_strain_pe_df, var = "Right Heart Strain Missingness")
colnames(rh_strain_pe_df)[2:3] <- c("PE Absent (0)", "PE Present (1)")

rh_strain_pe_df %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Cross-tabulation of Right Heart Strain Missingness by PE Status") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r}
merged_data %>%
  mutate(pe_status_num = as.numeric(as.character(pe_status)),
         rh_strain_missing = ifelse(is.na(rh_strain), "Missing", "Not Missing")) %>%
  group_by(rh_strain_missing) %>%
  summarise(pe_rate = mean(pe_status_num, na.rm = TRUE),
            n = n()) %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Pulmonary Embolism Rate by Right Heart Strain") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```


The diagnostic tests suggest that missingness in the `rh_strain` variable is consistent with a **Missing At Random (MAR)** framework which will be used to execute imputation of the missing values. To identify a robust set of covariates for the imputation model, all variables with **no missing values** were extracted from the dataset and a **Random Forest classifier** was trained on the complete cases of `rh_strain` using these variables to predict its presence or absence. The 10 variables to be considered including in the imputation model were ranked by **Mean Decrease in Accuracy**, a measure of their predictive importance.

```{r}
no_missing_vars <- names(merged_data)[colSums(is.na(merged_data)) == 0]
merged_data_no_missing <- merged_data[, no_missing_vars]
```

```{r}
formula_str <- paste(
  "rh_strain ~", 
  paste(no_missing_vars[no_missing_vars != "rh_strain"], collapse = " + ")
)
rf_formula <- as.formula(formula_str)

rf_data <- merged_data %>% filter(!is.na(rh_strain))

set.seed(123)
rf_model <- randomForest(
  formula = rf_formula,
  data = rf_data,
  importance = TRUE, 
  ntree = 500
)

var_importance <- importance(rf_model, type = 1) 
top_vars <- rownames(var_importance)[order(-var_importance[, 1])][1:10]

importance_df <- as.data.frame(importance(rf_model))
importance_df$Variable <- rownames(importance_df)

top10_vars <- importance_df %>%
  arrange(desc(MeanDecreaseAccuracy)) %>%
  select(Variable, MeanDecreaseAccuracy) %>%
  slice(1:10)

top10_vars %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Top 10 Predictors of Right Heart Strain (by Mean Decrease Accuracy)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

To impute missing values in `rh_strain`, we applied the same iterative approach used for previous variables, utilizing **Multiple Imputation by Chained Equations (MICE)** with logistic regression. The imputation model included `pe_status` and a targeted set of predictors identified via Random Forest variable importance on complete cases. The selected covariates (`well_score`, `revised_geneva_score`, `systolic`, `map_value`) demonstrated strong predictive value and had no missingness themselves. The code for the imputation iteration is not shown here.

Both models used the same covariates included in the imputation model. Results showed a non statistically significant effect of `rh_thrombus` on PE status in either model: 

- The coefficient for `rh_thrombus` changed only slightly from **-14.652 ** (pre-imputation) to **-15.281** (imputed), reinforcing that the imputation did not meaningfully alter the relationship between `rh_thrombus` and the outcome.

```{r}
impute_vars <- c("rh_thrombus", "dvt_pe", "revised_geneva_score", "elevated_bnp") 
logit_formula <- as.formula(paste("pe_status ~", paste(impute_vars, collapse = " + ")))

model_complete <- glm(logit_formula,
                      data = pre_imputation_data,
                      family = binomial)

model_imputed <- glm(logit_formula,
                     data = merged_data,
                     family = binomial)

summary_complete <- summary(model_complete)
summary_imputed <- summary(model_imputed)

logit_table <- data.frame(
  Coef_Complete = round(summary_complete$coefficients[, "Estimate"], 3),
  P_Complete = round(summary_complete$coefficients[, "Pr(>|z|)"], 3),
  Coef_Imputed = round(summary_imputed$coefficients[, "Estimate"], 3),
  P_Imputed = round(summary_imputed$coefficients[, "Pr(>|z|)"], 3)
)


logit_table_sorted <- logit_table[order(logit_table$P_Imputed), ]

logit_table_sorted %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Logistic Regression Comparison Between Pre and Post Imputated Data") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```



### Handling Missingness of rv_hypokines_on_echo

The variable `rv_hypokines_on_echo` has 39.89% missing data. To evaluate whether this missingness is related to the outcome variable `pe_status`, a cross-tabulation was performed. Among PE cases, 97 had observed `rv_hypokines_on_echo` values and 90 were missing; among non-PE individuals, 117 had observed values and 53 were missing. The proportion of missingness is vastly different between the two groups, suggesting that missingness is likely systematically associated with PE diagnosis.

To further investigate, the PE rate was compared between those with observed and missing `rv_hypokines_on_echo` data. The PE rate was 54.67% in the observed group and 37.06% in the missing group, showing notable difference. These patterns support the assumption that the missingness in `rv_hypokines_on_echo` is not consistent with a **Missing Completely At Random (MCAR)** mechanism.

```{r}
rv_hypokines_on_echo_pe_table <- table(is.na(merged_data$rv_hypokines_on_echo), merged_data$pe_status)
rv_hypokines_on_echo_pe_df <- as.data.frame.matrix(rv_hypokines_on_echo_pe_table)
rownames(rv_hypokines_on_echo_pe_df) <- c("Observed (Not Missing)", "Missing")
rv_hypokines_on_echo_pe_df <- tibble::rownames_to_column(rv_hypokines_on_echo_pe_df, var = "Right Ventricular Hypokinesis Missingness")
colnames(rv_hypokines_on_echo_pe_df)[2:3] <- c("PE Absent (0)", "PE Present (1)")

rv_hypokines_on_echo_pe_df %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Cross-tabulation of Right Ventricular Hypokinesis Missingness by PE Status") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```


```{r}
merged_data %>%
  mutate(pe_status_num = as.numeric(as.character(pe_status)),
         rv_hypokines_on_echo_missing = ifelse(is.na(rv_hypokines_on_echo), "Missing", "Not Missing")) %>%
  group_by(rv_hypokines_on_echo_missing) %>%
  summarise(pe_rate = mean(pe_status_num, na.rm = TRUE),
            n = n()) %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Pulmonary Embolism Rate by Right Ventricular Hypokinesis") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```


The diagnostic tests suggest that missingness in the `rv_hypokines_on_echo` variable is consistent with a **Missing At Random (MAR)** framework which will be used to execute imputation of the missing values. To identify a robust set of covariates for the imputation model, all variables with **no missing values** were extracted from the dataset and a **Random Forest classifier** was trained on the complete cases of `rv_hypokines_on_echo` using these variables to predict its presence or absence. The 10 variables to be considered including in the imputation model were ranked by **Mean Decrease in Accuracy**, a measure of their predictive importance.

```{r}
no_missing_vars <- names(merged_data)[colSums(is.na(merged_data)) == 0]
merged_data_no_missing <- merged_data[, no_missing_vars]
```

```{r}
formula_str <- paste(
  "rv_hypokines_on_echo ~", 
  paste(no_missing_vars[no_missing_vars != "rv_hypokines_on_echo"], collapse = " + ")
)
rf_formula <- as.formula(formula_str)

rf_data <- merged_data %>% filter(!is.na(rv_hypokines_on_echo))

set.seed(123)
rf_model <- randomForest(
  formula = rf_formula,
  data = rf_data,
  importance = TRUE, 
  ntree = 500
)

var_importance <- importance(rf_model, type = 1) 
top_vars <- rownames(var_importance)[order(-var_importance[, 1])][1:10]

importance_df <- as.data.frame(importance(rf_model))
importance_df$Variable <- rownames(importance_df)

top10_vars <- importance_df %>%
  arrange(desc(MeanDecreaseAccuracy)) %>%
  select(Variable, MeanDecreaseAccuracy) %>%
  slice(1:10)

top10_vars %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Top 10 Predictors of Right Ventricular Hypokinesis (by Mean Decrease Accuracy)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

To impute missing values in `rv_hypokines_on_echo`, we applied the same iterative approach used for previous variables, utilizing **Multiple Imputation by Chained Equations (MICE)** with logistic regression. The imputation model included `pe_status` and a targeted set of predictors identified via Random Forest variable importance on complete cases. The selected covariates (`map_value`, `rh_strain`, `elevated_bnp`) demonstrated strong predictive value and had no missingness themselves. The code for the imputation iteration is not shown here. 

The imputation process was performed across 5 datasets with 10 iterations each. The first completed dataset was used to fill in the missing `rv_hypokines_on_echo` values, ensuring consistency with observed data patterns and preserving relationships with key clinical variables.

```{r}
impute_vars <- c("pe_status", "rv_hypokines_on_echo", "map_value", "rh_strain", "elevated_bnp")
impute_data <- merged_data[, impute_vars]
```

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}
capture.output({
  imputed_data <- mice(
    impute_data,
    m = 5,
    method = "logreg",
    maxit = 10,
    seed = 123
  )
}, file = NULL)
```

```{r}
pre_imputation_data <- merged_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(rv_hypokines_on_echo))
```

```{r}
completed_data <- complete(imputed_data, 1)
merged_data$rv_hypokines_on_echo[is.na(merged_data$rv_hypokines_on_echo)] <- 
  completed_data$rv_hypokines_on_echo[is.na(merged_data$rv_hypokines_on_echo)]
```

**Sensitivity Analysis: Validating Imputation of rv_hypokines_on_echo ** 

**Distributional Consistency:** To validate the robustness of the imputation strategy, a sensitivity analysis was conducted to evaluate whether imputing missing values for `rv_hypokines_on_echo` preserved the integrity of the dataset. A bar plot comparing the proportions of `rv_hypokines_on_echo` values (0 vs. 1) between observed and imputed cases revealed closely aligned distributions. This suggests that the imputation procedure maintained the original variable structure and did not distort class proportions.

```{r}
merged_data %>%
  mutate(rv_hypokines_on_echo_flag = ifelse(is.na(impute_data$rv_hypokines_on_echo), "Imputed", "Observed")) %>%
  group_by(rv_hypokines_on_echo_flag, rv_hypokines_on_echo) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(rv_hypokines_on_echo_flag) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(rv_hypokines_on_echo), y = prop, fill = rv_hypokines_on_echo_flag)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  labs(title = "Proportion ofRight Ventricular Hypokinesis (Observed vs Imputed)",
       x = "rh_thrombus", y = "Proportion") +
  theme_minimal()
```

**Impact on Model Estimates: ** We further assessed the effect of imputation on model estimates by fitting logistic regression models predicting `pe_status` before and after imputation. Both models used the same covariates included in the imputation model. Results showed a statistically significant effect of `rv_hypokines_on_echo` on PE status in either model at the 0.05 significance level: 

- The coefficient for `rv_hypokines_on_echo` changed only slightly from **-1.185 ** (pre-imputation) to **-0.986** (imputed), reinforcing that the imputation did not meaningfully alter the relationship between `rv_hypokines_on_echo` and the outcome.

```{r}
impute_vars <- c( "rv_hypokines_on_echo", "map_value", "rh_strain", "elevated_bnp")
logit_formula <- as.formula(paste("pe_status ~", paste(impute_vars, collapse = " + ")))

model_complete <- glm(logit_formula,
                      data = pre_imputation_data,
                      family = binomial)

model_imputed <- glm(logit_formula,
                     data = merged_data,
                     family = binomial)

summary_complete <- summary(model_complete)
summary_imputed <- summary(model_imputed)

logit_table <- data.frame(
  Coef_Complete = round(summary_complete$coefficients[, "Estimate"], 3),
  P_Complete = round(summary_complete$coefficients[, "Pr(>|z|)"], 3),
  Coef_Imputed = round(summary_imputed$coefficients[, "Estimate"], 3),
  P_Imputed = round(summary_imputed$coefficients[, "Pr(>|z|)"], 3)
)


logit_table_sorted <- logit_table[order(logit_table$P_Imputed), ]

logit_table_sorted %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Logistic Regression Comparison Between Pre and Post Imputated Data") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

### Handling Missingness of echo_rvsp_value and rvsp_based_age

The variable `echo_rvsp_value`, which is a continuous measure of right ventricular systolic pressure exhibited **60.92% missingness**, identical to its binary counterpart `rvsp_based_age`.

A cross-tabulation showed the distribution of missingness by pulmonary embolism (PE) status:

- Among individuals **with PE**, 57 had observed `echo_rvsp_value` and 130 had missing entries.
- Among individuals **without PE**, 82 had observed values and 88 had missing.

The unequal proportions of missingness across the two groups suggest that the missingness may be strongly associated with PE status, supporting the assumption that the missingness of the `echo_rvsp_value` variable may not be **Missing Completely at Random (MCAR)**. 


```{r}
echo_pe_table <- table(is.na(merged_data$echo_rvsp_value), merged_data$pe_status)
echo_pe_df <- as.data.frame.matrix(echo_pe_table)
rownames(echo_pe_df) <- c("Observed (Not Missing)", "Missing")
echo_pe_df <- tibble::rownames_to_column(echo_pe_df, var = "Echo RVSP Missingness")
colnames(echo_pe_df)[2:3] <- c("PE Absent (0)", "PE Present (1)")
echo_pe_df %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Cross-tabulation of Echo RVSP Missingness by PE Status") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```


Furthermore, the conclusion that the missingness is MAR is supported by running two statistical tests:   
- **Chi-square test of independence** yielded a significant p-value of **0.0008771**, indicating no association between missingness and PE status.   
- **Little’s MCAR test** returned a p-value of **0.000591**, further supporting the MCAR assumption.  

```{r}
chisq.test(table(is.na(merged_data$echo_rvsp_value), merged_data$pe_status))
mcar_test(merged_data[,c("echo_rvsp_value","pe_status")]) 
```

**Logistic Regression Analysis of Missingness**

To further examine the mechanism behind the missing data, a logistic regression model was used to predict the binary indicator `missing_echo_rvsp_value` (1 = missing, 0 = observed), using only variables with complete data to avoid additional bias.

The results showed:
- **`pe_status` was a significant predictor** of missingness.  

This pattern suggests that the missingness of this variable may not appear random with respect to the outcome variable. Given these findings, **multiple imputation** was chosen over complete case analysis to preserve statistical power and reduce potential bias.

```{r}
merged_data$missing_echo_rvsp_value <- as.numeric(is.na(merged_data$echo_rvsp_value))
```

```{r}
no_missing_vars <- names(merged_data)[colSums(is.na(merged_data)) == 0]
merged_data_no_missing <- merged_data[, no_missing_vars]
```

```{r}
excluded_vars <- c("echo_rvsp_value", "missing_echo_rvsp_value", "rvsp_based_age")
predictor_vars <- setdiff(names(merged_data_no_missing), excluded_vars)

formula_str <- paste("missing_echo_rvsp_value ~", paste(predictor_vars, collapse = " + "))
formula <- as.formula(formula_str)

missingness_model <- glm(formula, data = merged_data_no_missing, family = binomial)

significant_vars <- tidy(missingness_model) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)", p.value < 0.1) %>%
  arrange(p.value)

significant_vars %>%
  mutate(p.value = signif(p.value, 3)) %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Significant Predictors of Missingness in echo_rvsp_value") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```


**Imputation of echo_rvsp_value: ** 

Missing values in `echo_rvsp_value` were imputed using **Predictive Mean Matching (PMM)** implemented via the `mice` package. To accommodate the skewed distribution of `echo_rvsp_value`, the variable was first log-transformed using `log1p()`. The imputation was performed over **5 datasets with 10 iterations each**, using the following predictors:

- Variables identified as significantly associated with missingness:  
  `acute_resp`, `haemoptysis`, `admission_year`, and `immobilization_surgery` (see table above).  
- Additional clinically and statistically relevant variables:    
  `pe_status`, `heart_rate`, `diastolic`, `systolic`.  

A predictor matrix was used to limit predictors to this predefined set. After imputation, the log-transformed values were back-transformed using `expm1()` to return to the original scale.

Finally, the binary variable `rvsp_based_age` was recalculated from the imputed values, where values > 40 mmHg were coded as 1 (positive), and ≤ 0.5 µg/mL as 0 (negative).

```{r}
mandatory_predictors <- c(
  "acute_resp", "haemoptysis", "immobilization_surgery", "pe_status", "admission_year"
)
clinical_predictors <- c(
  "heart_rate", "diastolic", "systolic")
  
  impute_predictors <- c(mandatory_predictors, clinical_predictors)
```

```{r}
merged_data$log_rvsp <- log1p(merged_data$echo_rvsp_value)
impute_data <- merged_data[, c("log_rvsp", impute_predictors)]
```

```{r}
pred_matrix <- make.predictorMatrix(impute_data)
pred_matrix[,] <- 0  
pred_matrix["log_rvsp", impute_predictors] <- 1
```

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}
capture.output(
  imp <- mice(impute_data,
              method = "pmm", 
              predictorMatrix = pred_matrix,
              m = 20, 
              maxit = 50,
              seed = 123),
  file = NULL
)
```

```{r}
log_rvsp<- complete(imp, 1)$log_rvsp
merged_data$echo_rvsp_value <- expm1(log_rvsp)

merged_data$echo_rvsp_value <- as.numeric(merged_data$echo_rvsp_value)
merged_data$rvsp_based_age <- factor(
  ifelse(merged_data$echo_rvsp_value > 40, 1, 0),
  levels = c(0, 1)
)
```

**Validation of Imputed echo_rvsp_value and derived rvsp_based_age ** 

The imputation of `echo_rvsp_value` was evaluated by comparing distributions between observed and imputed values. Summary statistics show similar central tendencies across groups: the **mean** values were 39.87 (observed) and 38.52 (imputed), and **median** values were 36. 

Statistical comparisons confirmed these similarities:  
- **Welch Two-Sample t-test**: *p* = 0.4984
- **Wilcoxon Rank-Sum test**: *p* = 0.4145  

Both p-values exceed 0.05, indicating no significant difference in means or distributions between the groups.

This conclusion is further supported by a **density plot**, which shows substantial overlap between observed and imputed distributions with no apparent shift. Together, these findings indicate that the imputation procedure effectively preserved the original data structure of the echo rvsp values and did not introduce systematic bias.

```{r}
imputed_df <- complete(imp, 1)
imputed_df$imputed_flag <- ifelse(is.na(merged_data$log_rvsp), "Imputed", "Observed")

imputed_df$echo_rvsp_value<- expm1(imputed_df$log_rvsp)

summary_table <- imputed_df %>%
  mutate(imputed_flag = factor(imputed_flag, levels = c("Observed", "Imputed"))) %>%
  group_by(imputed_flag) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean = round(mean(echo_rvsp_value, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    Median = round(median(echo_rvsp_value, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    SD = round(sd(echo_rvsp_value, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    N = n(),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

summary_table %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Summary of RVSP Levels by Imputation Status") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"))
```

```{r}
t.test(echo_rvsp_value ~ imputed_flag, data = imputed_df)
```


```{r}
wilcox.test(echo_rvsp_value ~ imputed_flag, data = imputed_df)
```

```{r}
ggplot(imputed_df, aes(x = echo_rvsp_value, fill = imputed_flag)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Observed vs. Imputed RVSP Levels",
    x = "RVSP Levels",
    y = "Density",
    fill = "Value Type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

merged_data <- merged_data %>% select(-log_rvsp)
merged_data <- merged_data %>% select(-missing_echo_rvsp_value) 
```

# Part D: Descriptive Statistics (Univariate) 

**Note: This analysis is run without the COVID-19 variable ** 

The `COVID-19` variable was intentionally excluded from this analysis due to important methodological considerations. The dataset includes patient records from 2019, a pre-pandemic period during which COVID-19 did not exist clinically, and diagnostic criteria were not yet established. Including the COVID-19 variable would introduce **temporal confounding**, as the variable is uniformly absent in 2019 and variably present from 2020 to 2023. This inconsistency could bias the model and obscure true associations. By excluding `COVID-19`, the analysis maintains temporal consistency across the dataset, thereby enhancing the generalizability and validity of the identified predictors. Further justification for this exclusion will be presented in subsequent sections when evaluating the key predictors associated with the log-odds of developing pulmonary embolism.

After removing the original COVID-19 variable, there are a total of 357 observations and 45 variables. 

```{r}

  select(-covid)
str(merged_data_no_covid) 
```

```{r binary_barplots_covid, fig.width=10, fig.height=29}
binary_vars <- categorical_vars[!categorical_vars %in% c("race", "heart_rate_geneva", "bmi_marker", "age_group")]

create_binary_barplot <- function(data, var_name) {
  plot_data <- data %>%
    count(!!sym(var_name)) %>%
    mutate(
      percentage = n / sum(n) * 100,
      label = paste0(n, "\n(", round(percentage, 1), "%)")
    )
  
  max_y <- ceiling(max(plot_data$n) / 100) * 100 

  ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = factor(!!sym(var_name)), y = n, fill = factor(!!sym(var_name)))) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_text(aes(label = label), vjust = -0.5, size = 3) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, max_y, by = 75), limits = c(0, max_y)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("0" = "#E74C3C", "1" = "#3498DB")) +
    labs(
      title = paste(var_name),
      x = var_name,
      y = "Count"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7)
    )
}

binary_plots <- map(binary_vars, ~ {
  if (.x %in% names(merged_data_no_covid)) {
    create_binary_barplot(merged_data_no_covid, .x)
  }
}) %>% compact()

grid_plots <- do.call("grid.arrange", c(binary_plots, ncol = 4))
```

30. `bmi_marker`: BMI Marker has 6 categories and is classified as - **Underweight: ** BMI less than 18.5, **Normal: ** BMI between 18.5-24.9, **Overweight: ** BMI betwen 25-29.9, **Obesity Class 1: ** 30-34.9, **Obesity Class 2:**  35-39.9, **Obesity Class 3: ** 40 or greater (also referred to as severe or morbid obesity)

```{r nonbinary_barplots_covid, fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
non_binary_vars <- c("race", "bmi_marker", "heart_rate_geneva", "age_group")
create_nonbinary_barplot <- function(data, var_name) {
  plot_data <- data %>%
    count(!!sym(var_name)) %>%
    mutate(

    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, max_y, by = 100), limits = c(0, max_y + max_y * 0.1)) +
    labs(
      title = paste(var_name),
      x = var_name,
      y = "Count"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8, angle = 45, hjust = 1)
    )
}

do.call("grid.arrange", c(nonbinary_plots, ncol = 2))
```
